source.name: Warosu Database Backup 2025-08-15
source.short-desc: Database backup of warosu.org on 2025-08-15 in mysqldump (SQL statements) format
source.capture:
12 per-board mysqldumps as .sql.zst (3, biz, cgl, ck, diy, fa, ic, jp, lit, sci, vr, vt -- same board set as 2023-03-15). The IA item lists them loose; an all-files zip of the same content also exists, so prepare handles either starting point. Uses extended inserts (many rows per INSERT statement), unlike 2023-03-15's one-INSERT-per-row: `grep -c '^INSERT INTO'` counts STATEMENTS here, not rows (1,393 vs 4,617,189 for cgl), and file sizes are not comparable across the two dumps -- cgl is 82MB smaller than 2023 purely because extended inserts strip ~25 bytes of per-row statement prefix, while actually holding 115,500 MORE posts.

This dump does NOT supersede 2023-03-15; both must stay ingested. Diffed distinct `num` per board across both dumps (2026-08-03, full scan of all 12 boards on both sides): adds 83,238,889 posts but LOSES 178,739 that 2023 has -- jp 116,122, lit 42,661, sci 18,630, fa 1,326. Because ingest is first-writer-wins and 2023 was ingested first, its copies are the ones retained.

Per-board new posts: vt 58,250,102, jp 6,911,621, biz 6,649,675, lit 2,849,534, ck 2,458,908, vr 1,988,217, sci 1,472,288, ic 1,128,096, fa 980,837, diy 357,209, cgl 115,500, 3 76,902. /vt/ more than doubled (41.4M -> 99.7M) and accounts for the whole 10GB -> 22GB growth of that file.

278,251,735 rows total, of which 381,415 are ghost posts (subnum != 0) and are skipped on ingest; 351,178 of those are on /jp/.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22 by a full `ingest-all --count-only` pass over the re-staged out/ tree (two independent runs, byte-identical totals): 278,071,446 real posts + 382,520 ghosts = 278,453,966 rows read, 7,291,864 OPs, 12 boards, ZERO undated and ZERO unparsable lines.

THE 278,251,735 FIGURE ABOVE IS AN UNDERCOUNT, by 202,231 rows (0.073%). It is kept rather than overwritten because the discrepancy is the point: this dump uses extended inserts, so it is exactly the one where `grep -c '^INSERT INTO'` counts statements and not rows, and whatever produced the old number could not have been a line count. The 2023-03-15 dump, where grep IS valid, agrees with its parse to 12 rows in 195M. A figure recorded without its method stated is not checkable; state the method next time. Ghosts were likewise 381,415, measured 382,520.
